requirements.title: Fixed configuration and native interfaces
requirements.definition: The default configuration is fixed at 4 s-side request ports and 4 m-side target ports, with DATA_WIDTH=32, ADDR_WIDTH=32, STRB_WIDTH=4, ID_WIDTH=8, each USER_WIDTH=1, all USER_ENABLE=0, FORWARD_ID=0, and M_REGIONS=1. Each M_ADDR_WIDTH=24, M_BASE_ADDR=0 uses automatic regions, all M_CONNECT_READ/WRITE connections are enabled, and M_SECURE=0. Lower port indices occupy the lower bits of packed vectors; do not change to 1×1 or enable user/ID forwarding.
requirements.scenario: Use the exact default configuration, with each of all 4 s ports issuing read and write transactions to each of the 4 m ports; assign distinct addresses, IDs, payloads, and attributes to different ports, and check routing and low-order indices in every legal valid window.

requirements.title: Synchronous reset and handshaking
requirements.definition: Sampling occurs on the rising edge of clk, and rst is an active-high synchronous reset. After a reset edge, all output ready and valid signals for AW/AR/W/B/R are cleared, and unfinished transactions are discarded; invalid payloads are not required to be cleared or held. Drives change on falling edges, and payload remains stable while valid waits for ready; a handshake is effective only on a rising edge where valid and ready are both 1; ready may change freely. Transactions restart after reset is deasserted, and legal inputs contain no X/Z.
requirements.scenario: First establish nonempty W/R buffers or a blocked B response through native transactions, then assert rst on a falling edge and hold it across multiple rising edges; check that there is no asynchronous clearing before the edge and that all ready/valid signals are 0 after the edge, then issue transactions again after release. Block each channel separately and hold valid and payload until handshaking.

requirements.title: Global arbitration and single-transaction serialization
requirements.definition: Only one transaction is serviced globally; among the 8 requests, index 2*n is AW for s[n], and 2*n+1 is AR. After reset, round-robin priority starts at the lowest index; after a selection, the next starting point is the selected index+1, wrapping around. The grant remains asserted until the corresponding s-side B handshake or Rlast handshake releases it. AW/AR completion must not release it early; simultaneous reads and writes and different request ports are serialized according to this rule.
requirements.scenario: Have all 4 s ports simultaneously hold AW and AR requests, marking the 8 requests with different addresses and IDs; complete data and responses according to the selected transaction, check the cyclic order, and block the final R beat or B to verify that other addresses cannot proceed ahead of it. Cover wraparound over two consecutive rounds.

requirements.title: Address acceptance and fixed latency
requirements.definition: When idle, a request first wins arbitration on one rising edge; on the next rising edge, the address fields are captured and the corresponding s_awready or s_arready is set to 1; the address handshake occurs on the following rising edge. Decoding occurs on that handshake edge; after the edge, a legal write enables the corresponding s_wready, and a legal read enables m_rready; the following rising edge generates the corresponding m_awvalid or m_arvalid. The m address valid remains asserted until a handshake with the target ready; a new address is accepted only at the next idle service opportunity after global response completion.
requirements.scenario: Issue one read or write request on a falling edge from idle, record address ready, decoding, and m address valid edge by edge, and separately insert multiple cycles of low m_awready/arready. Check the exact latency, that there is only one s address handshake, and that the m address fields are held.

requirements.title: Address regions and attribute forwarding
requirements.definition: The four target regions are, in order, 0x00000000–0x00ffffff, 0x01000000–0x01ffffff, 0x02000000–0x02ffffff, and 0x03000000–0x03ffffff; all other addresses miss. The target AW/AR address, len, size, burst, lock, cache, prot, and qos pass through the original request, with region=0, user=0, and downstream ID=0. Addresses are not incremented per beat or split; burst counting is maintained by the endpoints; valid is 0 for unselected targets.
requirements.scenario: For all s/m combinations, read and write the first and last addresses of each region and the adjacent boundaries; randomize all address attributes and include len0/1/3/255 and every legal burst value. Check that only the correct target has valid asserted and check all pass-through attributes; separately test read and write misses outside the regions.

requirements.title: Write data buffering and backpressure
requirements.definition: The selected write transaction receives W from the corresponding s port, and Wdata/strb/last are sent in order to the selected m port, with Wuser fixed at 0. The W path has an elastic capacity of two beats; a handshaken beat may become m_wvalid after that edge. Valid output payload remains stable when blocked, and beats must not be lost, duplicated, or reordered. s_wready is a registered output; target ready or a buffer slot still unoccupied after the update is the condition for enabling it on the next cycle; acceptance under the current ready determines whether data enters the buffer on this edge. After receiving Wlast, stop receiving W for this transaction and switch to waiting for B.
requirements.scenario: Perform multibeat write bursts for all s/m combinations, with distinct data and strb values of 0/single byte/full word and random values, separately sending consecutive beats and inserting valid gaps. Keep m_wready low initially to fill two beats, then assert it on alternate cycles; hold the beat while the source is blocked, and check capacity, latency, ordering, and Wlast occurring exactly once.

requirements.title: Write response routing
requirements.definition: Enable the selected m_bready after the edge that receives upstream Wlast; legal endpoints provide B only after the target AW and all W have handshaken. After the downstream B handshake, set Bvalid for the selected s port after the edge, passing Bresp through, using the original AWID rather than m_bid for Bid, and setting Buser=0. While s_bready is low, hold Bvalid and the valid payload; the final s-side B handshake releases arbitration, and no Bvalid appears on other s ports.
requirements.scenario: Use different IDs for write requests, deliberately make m_bid differ from the request, and exercise Bresp values 00/01/10/11. Delay B and hold the response while s_bready is low; check the actual source ID, target uniqueness, and that other requests are blocked during the wait.

requirements.title: Read data buffering and responses
requirements.definition: The selected read transaction receives R only from the selected m port; Rdata/resp/last pass through beat by beat to the original s port, with Rid always equal to the original ARID rather than m_rid, and Ruser=0. The R path has an elastic capacity of two beats; valid payload remains stable when blocked, and beats must not be lost, duplicated, or reordered; upstream ready and capacity determine the registered m_rready. After receiving the target Rlast, stop receiving downstream R, and release arbitration only after this final beat handshakes on the s side; normal reads do not independently generate or truncate data based on ARLEN.
requirements.scenario: For all s/m combinations, read 1/2/4/8/256 beats, with distinct data/resp per beat and deliberately different downstream IDs. Combine continuous R and gapped R with low upstream ready to fill two beats, then release and apply alternating backpressure; check ordering, last, source ID, and that blocking the final beat does not release the transaction.

requirements.title: Read miss returns
requirements.definition: An address miss sends no AR to any m port. Internally generate ARLEN+1 R beats, with data 0, resp=2'b11 meaning DECERR, Rid equal to the request ID, and user0; only the final beat has last1. Observe the same R buffering and upstream backpressure; the transaction completes after all beats are received, and the count must not overflow while incrementing and cause unlimited transmission.
requirements.scenario: Have the four s ports read out-of-region addresses with len0/1/3/255, keeping m_rvalid at 0. Keep s_rready low initially, then accept intermittently; use independent counting to check exactly len+1 beats, the final marker, 0data, and DECERR, and check that no m_arvalid is asserted.

requirements.title: Write miss discarding and responses
requirements.definition: An address miss sends no AW or W to any m port. Receive and discard W from the selected s port, returning one B to that s port only after the Wlast handshake, with resp=2'b11 meaning DECERR, Bid equal to the original AWID, and user0. AWLEN does not replace the Wlast termination condition; hold the response under upstream B backpressure.
requirements.scenario: Perform out-of-region writes of 1/multiple beats and insert valid gaps before Wlast, deliberately making AWLEN differ from the Wlast position. Check that there are no downstream AW/W handshakes, no B before last, and only one DECERR after last; block B, then release it and issue the next transaction.

requirements.title: read-ready target during decoding
requirements.definition: In the first cycle after a legal read address handshake, the onehot position of m_rready uses the target index saved from the previous decoding, with an initial value of 0 at the start of simulation; synchronous reset does not clear the saved target index, and the reset edge still commits the index obtained from combinational decoding before reset. The subsequent first beat projects according to this historical index; from the next cycle onward, use the current target index. Validity is determined by the read buffer availability condition at that time. Legal endpoints do not send R before the corresponding AR handshake, so this ready projection cannot create data from nothing; this clause only specifies the exact timing of public control outputs.
requirements.scenario: Alternate targets 0/1/3/2 in consecutive reads, keeping m_rvalid at 0 before AR. Compare edge by edge the old ready target on the first cycle after decoding and the new target on the next cycle; send R only after the target AR completes. For the first read after the initial reset, select a nonzero target to check the initial value of 0; reset again after a history containing a nonzero target to check index retention, and cover the case where decoding is in progress before the reset edge.

requirements.title: Valid windows and four-state comparisons
requirements.definition: All output ready/valid signals are meaningful in both the pre-edge and post-edge stable windows of every edge after reset has occurred; payload is valid only when its port's valid is 1. Payload may show the same value on multiple ports; payload on unselected ports with valid0 is not scored and is not required to be 0. Differences in valid must be reported independently as errors; control mismatches must not be masked because actual or expected valid is 0; X/Z at valid points is an error.
requirements.scenario: Compare cycle by cycle under combinations of valid0/1 and backpressure on all channels. Compare ready/valid independently for each port, compare payload only when both sides have valid1, check the current handshake before the edge, and wait 1ns after the edge to compare updates. Report errors for valid mismatches and valid X/Z values.
